description: Per-country fNRB for ex-ante calculations and the transition analysis, structured by VINTAGE. The OFFICIAL source for national defaults is A6.4-AMT-009 v01.0 Table 3 (Amy's ruling (2), 2026-09-21), whose values are the same as CDM TOOL33 v03.0 Table 3 (AMT-009 para.16) and originate in MoFuSS / Ghilardi & Bailis (2024); the default vintage carries exactly those values. Each value carries its vintage + citation; every calculator output MUST label which vintage was used. Missing country within a vintage -> the OFFICIAL multi-national value from A6.4-AMT-009 v01.0 Table 2, chosen by the country's UN M49 region (Amy's ruling (3), built 2026-09-22, calculator v0.10.0); a country outside the three regions gets no number and an honest refusal. STRUCK 2026-09-22: 'the labeled conservative global fallback' - the quartile dial is retired for fNRB. Transitioning projects supply their filing-era fNRB via per-project filed-override fields (entered + cited per project), NOT from these tables. See the vintage policy in notes.

ruleUpdate.label: fNRB rule update
ruleUpdate.instrument: A6.4-AMT-009 v01.0 (in force 21 May 2026, valid to 20 May 2029) Table 3 national and Table 2 multi-national fNRB defaults, pp.5-7; the same values as CDM TOOL33 v03.0, EB 125 Annex 2 (12 June 2025), Table 3 pp.5-7 (AMT-009 para.16); origin MoFuSS / Ghilardi & Bailis (2024), the national (adm0) dataset, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18865904
ruleUpdate.previousInstrument: CDM TOOL33 v02.0, EB 115 Annex 5 (8 September 2022), which introduced the earlier national defaults. Not held in Methodology/. CLOSED 2026-09-21 by Amy's ruling (1): the old-file hunt is over - transitioning projects use their filed value only, and no earlier-default line is built or planned.
ruleUpdate.desc: The report's separate 'fNRB rule update (<year>)' line reads its year from `effective` and its citation from `instrument`. The line is the legacy (V1.0) ER at the project's FILED fNRB minus the legacy ER at the current standardised-tool value; it is null, with a reason, when no filed value is on the record (Amy's amended R1, 2026-09-21). It sits OUTSIDE the methodology-transition table, which holds fNRB equal on both sides.
ruleUpdate.instrument_corrected_2026-09-22: STRUCK (Amy's ruling (2), 2026-09-21; corrected 2026-09-22): the line used to end 'Both take the MoFuSS June 2024 values (Table 5 pp.32-33)'. False - the tools' values match the MoFuSS adm0 dataset, not the June 2024 report's Table 5 (India 7 vs 6, Kenya 29 vs 30, Uganda 39 vs 35, Malawi 48 vs 49, Niger 61 vs 60; Tanzania 51 both). Kept here as the record of what was believed from 2026-09-21.

mofuss-2024-06-report.label: MoFuSS - June 2024 report (Table 5) - HISTORICAL, not the default
mofuss-2024-06-report.cite: MoFuSS, Updated fNRB Values for Woodfuel Interventions (20 Jun 2024), Table 5 national fNRB 2020-2030, pp.32-33
mofuss-2024-06-report.coverage: 6 anchor countries hand-keyed from the report's Table 5 (pp.32-33). HISTORICAL since 2026-09-22: the official tools took the adm0 dataset, not Table 5, so this vintage differs from A6.4-AMT-009 Table 3 on 5 of the 6 (IND 0.06 vs 0.07, KEN 0.30 vs 0.29, UGA 0.35 vs 0.39, MWI 0.49 vs 0.48, NER 0.60 vs 0.61; TZA 0.51 both). Kept as a cited record, read by no default path. STRUCK: 'The reference entries are anchored to THIS vintage' - they anchor to the official Table 3 values from calculator v0.9.0 (Amy's ruling (4)).

IND.name: India
IND.note: Genuinely-low case (fNRB 2020-2030 = 6%, report p.31). Large base of GS safe-water projects.

KEN.name: Kenya
KEN.note: Text-confirmed in the report: decreased from 46% to 30%.

UGA.name: Uganda
UGA.note: Flagship transition case: a documented pre-MoFuSS national default (2012-2017), higher than MoFuSS 0.35. That older value is filing-era; supply it per project via filed-override, not this table (vintage policy).

NER.name: Niger
NER.note: High-fNRB case (Sahel); spans the high end.

retired_2026-09-22_fallback.struck: STRUCK 2026-09-22 (Amy's ruling (3), 2026-09-21). The quartile dial is retired for fNRB on every vintage: a country with no national row takes A6.4-AMT-009 Table 2's official multi-national value for its UN M49 region, or gets an honest refusal outside the three regions. A quartile of the countries that happen to be in a table was never a published default - it was our own statistic, offered as if it were one. Kept here as the record of what was read until calculator v0.10.0; read by nothing.
retired_2026-09-22_fallback.cite: MoFuSS - June 2024 report (Table 5) — quartiles of the vintage's national fNRB. Lower fNRB = lower baseline = fewer credits = conservative; the 25th percentile is the default when a country is absent.
retired_2026-09-22_fallback.note: Adjustable Low/Median/High stops exposed by the UI ONLY when this fallback fires.

mofuss-adm0-csv.label: A6.4-AMT-009 Table 3 (national default)
mofuss-adm0-csv.cite: A6.4-AMT-009 v01.0 Table 3, national default values for fNRB (pp.5-7) - the same values as CDM TOOL33 v03.0 (EB 125 Annex 2, 12 June 2025) Table 3 (AMT-009 para.16); origin MoFuSS / Ghilardi & Bailis (2024), summary_adm0.csv column fNRB_2020_2030_mean, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18865904. Verified 2026-09-22: all 90 rows equal both tools' Table 3 exactly.
mofuss-adm0-csv.coverage: All 90 countries of A6.4-AMT-009 Table 3 (= TOOL33 v03.0 Table 3 = the MoFuSS adm0 dataset). DEFAULT vintage for new ex-ante calculations and, since 2026-09-22 (Amy's ruling (4)), the vintage the reference dataset anchors to. Countries absent take the official Table 2 multi-national value for their UN M49 region, or - outside the three regions - no number and an honest refusal (Amy's ruling (3), BUILT 2026-09-22, calculator v0.10.0). STRUCK: 'Countries absent fall back to the labelled quartile dial today; ruling (3) replaces that ... next sitting.'

multiNational.desc: THE OFFICIAL FALLBACK (Amy's ruling (3), 2026-09-21). A country with no Table 3 national row takes the multi-national value for its region. The region is decided by the cited UN M49 geoscheme in calculators/data/regions/un-m49.json, because AMT-009 names the three regions and publishes no country list for them. A country in none of the three takes NO VALUE - the calculator refuses and asks for a filed value.
multiNational.cite: A6.4-AMT-009 v01.0 Table 2, default values for fNRB at multi-national level (p.4) - the same values as CDM TOOL33 v03.0 Table 2 (AMT-009 para.16); origin MoFuSS / Ghilardi & Bailis (2024). Read from the PDF 2026-09-22.
multiNational.footnote5: A6.4-AMT-009 footnote 5: multi-national values are appropriate where no country-specific national value exists and the activity reduces charcoal use; they may also suit places where cross-border charcoal trade is pervasive and the multi-national value is conservative against the national one.
multiNational.noGlobalValue: CHECKED IN BOTH PRIMARY PDFs, 2026-09-22 (Amy asked, on her eyeball of ruling (3)): NEITHER TOOL PUBLISHES A GLOBAL OR WORLD fNRB ROW. A6.4-AMT-009 v01.0 Table 2 has exactly three rows (Asia, Latin America, Sub-Saharan Africa) and the word "global" does not appear anywhere in the document; CDM TOOL33 v03.0 Table 2 is titled "Regional (Continental) fNRB values" and carries the same three rows, with no global or world row either. Table 4 is SUB-national - narrower, not broader. So there is no wider official value being withheld from a project outside the three regions: the refusal is the whole of what the tools offer, not our choice among options.
multiNational.supportingRule: CDM TOOL33 v03.0 para.16: national values are the general choice, and a regional value is allowed only when no national value exists. Read 2026-09-22 - it states the national-then-regional order this fallback implements. AMT-009 footnote 5 is the CONDITION on using a regional value and is the one printed to the user; this line is the order-of-preference, recorded so the check is not repeated.
multiNational.refusal: No official fNRB default covers this country. AMT-009 publishes national values for 90 countries and multi-national values for three regions only; this country is in neither list, so the calculator has no number to offer and will not invent one.

notes: VINTAGE POLICY (standing; amended 2026-09-21 by Amy's amended R1; amended again 2026-09-21 by her ruling (1)): vintages are demand-driven, not exhaustive. Do NOT catalog historical fNRB sources as calculation vintages. Transitioning projects supply their filing-era fNRB from their own filed documents via per-project filed-override fields (entered + cited per project), not from lookup tables. Lookup tables serve ex-ante calculations on current vintages. STRUCK 2026-09-22 (ruling (1), the old-file hunt is closed): the 'ONE planned exception - an ILLUSTRATIVE earlier-default line read from TOOL33 v02.0' is withdrawn; transitioning projects use their filed value only.

Default vintage for new ex-ante = mofuss-adm0-csv (the A6.4-AMT-009 Table 3 values, full coverage). CORRECTED 2026-09-22: this line used to say 'The UI exposes a vintage picker (advanced area)' - no picker exists; the seat always uses defaultVintage, and a filed current value is the only override.

Reference entries anchor to the OFFICIAL Table 3 values (A6.4-AMT-009 = TOOL33 v03.0) from calculator v0.9.0, 2026-09-22 (Amy's ruling (4)): IND 0.07 / KEN 0.29 / UGA 0.39 / MWI 0.48 / TZA 0.51 / NER 0.61; 29 reference entries re-derived, table in the maintainers' reference derivation notes. STRUCK: 'Reference entries stay anchored to the report vintage; the exact-anchor gate passes within that vintage (IND 0.06 / KEN 0.30 / UGA 0.35 / MWI 0.49 / TZA 0.51 / NER 0.60). No reference re-derivation.'

B1 transition analysis computes under the filing-era values (via overrides) AND the latest vintage side by side. 'Which vintage validators accept for issuance' is on the reviewer's question list (Q1). Since 2026-09-21 the fNRB change is reported as its own 'fNRB rule update' line, apart from the methodology transition (see ruleUpdate).
Every calculator output MUST label the fNRB vintage used.

RULING (3), BUILT 2026-09-22 (calculator v0.10.0; was recorded here as NOT BUILT on 2026-09-22 and is struck to BUILT the same day): a country with no Table 3 row takes the official multi-national value from A6.4-AMT-009 Table 2 (Asia 18, Latin America 32, Sub-Saharan Africa 40) by the cited UN M49 geoscheme data file calculators/data/regions/un-m49.json; a country outside the three regions gets an honest 'no official default, enter a filed value' and no number; when a regional value is used the report prints AMT-009 footnote 5's condition (multi-national values are for activities reducing charcoal use where no national value exists). The quartile dial is retired for fNRB on every vintage - see each vintage's retired_2026-09-22_fallback. The dial itself stays for household size, which has no official regional table.
